html:
Here is a wide-field image of the neighborhood of the planetary nebula Messier 27 (the small red and green spot at lower left of the image.

First observed by Charles Messier on July 12, 1764, Messier 27 (Dumbbell Nebula) is located about 1200 light-years away in the constellation Vulpecula (the Little Fox). This nebula is the result of the explosion of a star 3000 to 4000 years ago. The star is now a white dwarf.



Here is an enlargement of the nebula.



Technical details
Telescope: Takahashi SKY90 II with dedicated f 4.5 focal reducer (407mm focal length)
Sensor: Canon 40D unfiltered
Filter: IDAS-LPS (to counter light pollution)
Mount: LX200 10" f 6.3 classic
Guiding: DSI pro and PHD

49 frames of 240 seconds, 40 darks, 20 flats
Stacking in DeepSkyStacker
Processing in photoshop
